canonical_data: two SQLite files per session, one per writer, plus per-agent workspace folders holding CLAUDE.md instructions and memory
current_repo_note: The README calls it an AI assistant, but what it ships is a self-hosted agent runtime with no conversational workspace of its own; it is catalogued with the other claw-family runtimes.
strengths: Each agent runs in its own Linux container with only explicitly mounted folders, so shell access is bounded by the container rather than by permission checks
A credential gateway injects keys at request time and enforces per-agent policies and rate limits, so agents never hold raw API keys
The architecture is small and documented: a host router, two single-writer SQLite files per session, and scheduled tasks with optional gates that skip waking the agent
weaknesses: The trunk is Anthropic-native; channels and other model providers are skills that copy code into each fork, so every installation diverges
Setup and customisation lean on Claude Code, which the README lists as a requirement
The README documents no approval step before an agent acts, and an optional hosted account unlocks a prebuilt image and managed Slack app
why_it_matters: A deliberately small, container-isolated runtime that makes the case for OS-level isolation over application-level permission checks in personal agents.
